target_skill: Deep physical understanding of all 5 phases of the SK-EFT Hawking radiation research program

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Lagrangian & Hamiltonian Mechanics
vertices.description: The variational principle, Euler-Lagrange equations, Hamiltonians, phase space, and Noether's theorem linking symmetries to conservation laws. The foundation for all field theory.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain why the action principle gives equations of motion, connect Noether's theorem to a physical symmetry, and articulate why Lagrangians are central to modern physics
vertices.example: In the project: Son's superfluid EFT L=P(X) is a Lagrangian. Understanding why phonon physics follows from extremizing the action of P(X) requires this foundation.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Quantum Mechanics Foundations
vertices.description: Wave-particle duality, Hilbert spaces, operators, the Schrödinger equation, path integrals, and the measurement problem. Emphasis on the path integral formulation as the bridge to QFT.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain path integrals physically (sum over histories), articulate why quantum mechanics uses complex amplitudes, and connect the Schrödinger equation to the Madelung transform
vertices.example: The Madelung transform ψ = √ρ exp(iS/ℏ) maps the Schrödinger equation to a compressible fluid — the starting point of the feasibility study.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Statistical Mechanics & Thermal Physics
vertices.description: Partition functions, ensembles, the Boltzmann distribution, free energy, entropy, phase transitions, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Essential for understanding thermal equilibrium in the SK context.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the fluctuation-dissipation theorem physically, describe what thermal equilibrium means at the microscopic level, and articulate why temperature appears in the KMS condition
vertices.example: The KMS condition ψ_a → ψ_a + iβ∂_t ψ_r in the SK formalism directly encodes thermal equilibrium at temperature T=1/β — this requires understanding what thermal equilibrium means statistically.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Fluid Dynamics Fundamentals
vertices.description: Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, compressible vs incompressible flow, sound waves, viscosity, and transport coefficients. The physical substrate for analog gravity.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain physically why sound waves exist in fluids, what viscosity does to wave propagation, and how supersonic flow creates horizons
vertices.example: The transonic background in transonic_background.py — a BEC flowing from subsonic to supersonic — is fundamentally a fluid dynamics problem. The sonic horizon is where v(x) = c_s(x).

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: EFT Philosophy & Derivative Expansion
vertices.description: The Wilsonian paradigm: physics at different scales decouples; low-energy physics is described by the most general action compatible with symmetries, organized by a derivative expansion. Power counting, naturalness, and UV/IR separation.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain to a non-physicist why EFT works (we don't need to know everything to make predictions), articulate what the derivative expansion physically means, and explain why higher-order terms are suppressed
vertices.example: The entire SK-EFT program is built on this: at first order in derivatives, there are 2 transport coefficients. At second order, 2 more. The counting formula count(N) = ⌊(N+1)/2⌋ + 1 follows from this philosophy.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Son's Superfluid EFT: L = P(X)
vertices.description: The leading-order effective field theory for a superfluid: a single Goldstone boson ψ with Lagrangian L = P(X), X = (∂ψ)². The equation of state determines all phonon interactions. Phonon field π defined by ψ = μt + π.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain why a superfluid is described by a single scalar field (spontaneous U(1) breaking → Goldstone), how P(X) encodes the equation of state, and why the sound speed is c_s² = P'/(P' + 2μ²P'')
vertices.example: Basic.lean defines the EFT structures. The acoustic metric theorem in AcousticMetric.lean proves that phonons propagate on g_acoustic — a direct consequence of expanding P(X) around the background.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking & Goldstone Modes
vertices.description: When the ground state has less symmetry than the Lagrangian, massless Goldstone bosons appear — one for each broken continuous symmetry. The phonon is the Goldstone of broken U(1) in a superfluid. Extends to non-Abelian SSB and the Higgs mechanism.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the Mexican hat potential analogy, why Goldstone modes are massless, and how the phonon in a superfluid is a Goldstone boson of broken U(1) particle number symmetry
vertices.example: In the ADW mechanism (Paper 5): GL(4,ℝ) → SO(3,1) breaking gives 16-6 = 10 broken generators. The graviton emerges as a Goldstone boson — this is SSB applied to spacetime symmetry.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: BEC Physics & Bogoliubov Theory
vertices.description: Bose-Einstein condensation, the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, Bogoliubov transformation for quasiparticles, healing length ξ, and the dispersion relation ω² = c²k² + ℏ²k⁴/4m². The microscopic basis for the analog gravity experiments.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain what a BEC is physically, why the healing length sets the EFT cutoff, what the Bogoliubov dispersion means for phonon propagation, and how P(X) = (X-m²)²/4λ gives GP in the non-relativistic limit
vertices.example: constants.py defines ξ, c_s, and scattering lengths for Steinhauer ⁸⁷Rb, Heidelberg ³⁹K, and Trento ²³Na. The healing length ξ = ℏ/mc_s is where the EFT breaks down.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: The Acoustic Metric & Analog Gravity
vertices.description: Unruh (1981) and Visser: sound waves in a moving fluid propagate on an effective curved spacetime. The acoustic metric g_μν = (ρ/c_s)·[matrix involving v and c_s]. Sonic horizons form where v = c_s. This is a rigorous theorem, not an analogy.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can derive (or follow the derivation of) the acoustic metric from linearized fluid equations, explain physically why supersonic flow creates a horizon, and articulate the limitations (kinematic only, no Einstein equations)
vertices.example: AcousticMetric.lean proves 4 theorems: det g = -ρ², inverse identity, Lorentzian signature, and phonon EOM = □_g π. These are the formal backbone of Paper 1.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Hawking Radiation & the Trans-Planckian Problem
vertices.description: Unruh's 1981 prediction: a sonic horizon emits thermal phonons at T_H = ℏκ/2πk_B, where κ is the surface gravity (velocity gradient at the horizon). The trans-Planckian problem: Hawking quanta trace back to exponentially blue-shifted modes — does UV physics matter?
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain why horizons radiate (mode mixing at the horizon), what the trans-Planckian problem is and why it matters, and why BEC experiments are the ideal testing ground
vertices.example: The entire program's raison d'être: Paper 1 shows that T_H is robust against dissipative UV modifications — δ_diss is small — directly addressing the trans-Planckian problem.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Transonic Flow & Sonic Horizons in BEC
vertices.description: Setting up the 1D transonic background: velocity v(x) and density n(x) satisfying Euler + continuity, with v(x_H) = c_s(x_H) at the horizon. Surface gravity κ = dv/dx|_H + dc_s/dx|_H. Experimental parameters for Steinhauer, Heidelberg, Trento.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the physical setup of a BEC sonic black hole, what surface gravity κ means physically, and why the adiabaticity parameter D = κξ/c_s controls the EFT validity
vertices.example: transonic_background.py solves this numerically using a tanh velocity profile. The three experimental setups (Rb-87, K-39, Na-23) define the parameter space.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: The Schwinger-Keldysh Contour
vertices.description: Why double the degrees of freedom? The SK contour runs forward in time (branch 1) then backward (branch 2) to compute real-time correlation functions in a mixed/thermal state. Physical fields ψ_r = (ψ_1+ψ_2)/2 and noise fields ψ_a = ψ_1 - ψ_2.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the physical motivation for the SK contour (computing expectation values in a thermal/mixed state), what the r and a fields represent physically, and why this formalism naturally includes both dissipation and noise
vertices.example: SKDoubling.lean formalizes this: the action I_SK[ψ_r, ψ_a] with 9 candidate terms at first order, constrained by normalization, positivity, and KMS.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: KMS Symmetry & Fluctuation-Dissipation Relations
vertices.description: The Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition encodes thermal equilibrium: ψ_a → ψ_a + iβ∂_t ψ_r. This generates the fluctuation-dissipation relation automatically — dissipation and noise are not independent but linked by temperature. The CGL dynamical KMS transformation.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain FDR in physical terms (if you push a system, the thermal fluctuations push back proportionally), why KMS is the symmetry statement of thermal equilibrium, and the key discovery: FirstOrderKMS correcting the original KMSSymmetry
vertices.example: The Aristotle-discovered counterexample c=(0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1,0) that broke the original KMS — and the corrected FirstOrderKMS. Also CGLTransform.lean deriving FDR from the CGL master formula.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: SK Axioms: Normalization, Positivity, KMS
vertices.description: The three axioms constraining the SK effective action: (1) Normalization: I_SK vanishes when ψ_a = 0. (2) Positivity: Im I_SK ≥ 0 (unitarity/probability conservation). (3) KMS: the dynamical KMS symmetry enforces thermal equilibrium. Together these determine the action up to transport coefficients.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain each axiom physically, why positivity implies probability conservation, and how the three axioms together reduce the 9 candidate first-order terms to 2 free transport coefficients (γ₁, γ₂)
vertices.example: SKDoubling.lean proves firstOrder_positivity (Im I_SK ≥ 0 from γ₁,₂ ≥ 0) and firstOrder_uniqueness (KMS + positivity → 2 free parameters).

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: First-Order Dissipative Hawking Correction
vertices.description: The central result of Phase 1: T_eff = T_H(1 + δ_disp + δ_diss + δ_cross), where δ_diss = Γ_H/κ is the NEW dissipative correction. The damping rate Γ_H depends on γ₁, γ₂. For BEC experiments, δ_diss ~ 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³ — small but nonzero, addressing the trans-Planckian problem.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the physical meaning of each correction (dispersive vs dissipative vs cross), why δ_diss being small is good news for the trans-Planckian problem, and what the spin-sonic enhancement factor means for experiments
vertices.example: HawkingUniversality.lean proves the combined universality theorem. formulas.py computes δ_diss for each experimental platform.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Transport Coefficient Counting & Higher Orders
vertices.description: At EFT order N, the number of independent dissipative transport coefficients is count(N) = ⌊(N+1)/2⌋ + 1. Second order adds 2 new coefficients requiring broken parity. The parity alternation theorem: odd orders are parity-preserving, even orders require parity breaking.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain physically why parity matters (the background flow breaks spatial parity at the horizon), what the counting formula means for the EFT program, and why the on-shell vanishing of δ^(2) is significant
vertices.example: enumeration.py validates the counting; SecondOrderSK.lean proves the formula. ThirdOrderSK.lean proves parity alternation for general N.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Frequency-Dependent Spectral Distortion
vertices.description: At second order, the Hawking spectrum develops a frequency-dependent correction δ^(2)(ω) ∝ ω³ — the spectrum is no longer purely Planckian. The positivity constraint γ_{2,1} + γ_{2,2} = 0 causes this to vanish on the acoustic shell; it's nonzero only via off-shell Bogoliubov dispersion.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain why a frequency-dependent correction is qualitatively different from a temperature shift, what on-shell vanishing means physically, and why spin-sonic systems might make this observable
vertices.example: wkb_analysis.py computes the spectral distortion. The on-shell vanishing was discovered during Aristotle Round 4.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: CGL Dynamical KMS Derivation
vertices.description: The Crossley-Glorioso-Liu master formula: K_N(ω,k) = -i[K_R(ω,k) - K_R(-ω,k)]/(β₀ω). This pairs noise with odd-in-ω dissipative terms, not conservative terms. The chain: CGL FDR → T-reversal → model identification → FirstOrderKMS.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the physical content of the CGL formula (noise comes from the antisymmetric part of the retarded kernel), why even-ω terms produce zero noise, and how this resolves the model restructuring from Phase 2D
vertices.example: cgl_derivation.py implements the SymPy derivation. CGLTransform.lean proves 7 theorems including cgl_implies_secondOrderKMS.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: WKB Connection Formula & Complex Turning Points
vertices.description: The exact WKB method for the dissipative mode equation: complex turning point shift δx_imag = Γ_H/(κ·c_s), Stokes line geometry, modified Bogoliubov coefficients. Three non-perturbative effects: modified unitarity |α|²-|β|²=1-δ_k, FDR noise floor, spectral floor.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain what a complex turning point means physically, why unitarity is modified by dissipation, what the FDR noise floor represents (KMS-mandated thermal noise independent of Hawking process), and why the spectral floor matters experimentally
vertices.example: Paper 4 (WKBConnection.lean, 17 theorems). The noise floor n_noise = δ_k/2 dominates Hawking radiation at ω ≳ 6T_H for Steinhauer.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Bogoliubov Coefficients & Particle Creation
vertices.description: When mode mixing occurs at a horizon, the vacuum of one observer contains particles seen by another. The Bogoliubov transformation connects in-modes to out-modes: |β_k|² gives the particle number spectrum. The standard Hawking result: n_k = 1/(e^{2πω/κ} - 1) = Planck distribution.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain physically how mode mixing creates particles, what |β_k|² represents, and why the Planck distribution emerges from horizon physics
vertices.example: bogoliubov.py computes modified coefficients with broken unitarity. WKBConnection.lean formalizes the modified unitarity relation.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Higher-Form Symmetries & Gauge Structure
vertices.description: Generalized symmetries where the conserved charge lives on a p-dimensional submanifold (p-form symmetry). 0-form = ordinary symmetry. 1-form = acts on line operators (Wilson loops). Key fact: higher-form symmetries must be Abelian — operators on codimension >1 submanifolds commute.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain what a 1-form symmetry is physically, why higher-form symmetries must be Abelian (operators on submanifolds commute), and what the photon is (Goldstone of broken magnetic 1-form symmetry)
vertices.example: GaugeErasure.lean: the photonization theorem. The photon survives hydrodynamization because U(1) has a genuine 1-form symmetry.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Non-Abelian Gauge Erasure Theorem
vertices.description: Non-Abelian gauge DOF are universally erased by hydrodynamization. The mechanism: non-Abelian groups have at most discrete Z_N center symmetries; breaking these produces domain walls, not Goldstone bosons. U(1) survives (photonization). This is the most important negative result of the program.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the full argument chain, why N=4 SYM is the decisive case, the Standard Model analysis (SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) → only U(1)_EM survives), and why this is a theorem not a conjecture
vertices.example: Paper 3 (GaugeErasure.lean, 11 theorems + 1 axiom). erasure_theorem.py with Standard Model and N=4 SYM analysis.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: ADW Mechanism: Emergent Tetrad Gravity
vertices.description: The Akama-Diakonov-Wetterich mechanism: a multi-fermion interaction produces a tetrad condensate ⟨e^a_μ⟩ ≠ 0 via spontaneous symmetry breaking GL(4,ℝ) → SO(3,1). The 10 broken generators give 6 massive spin-connection modes + 2 massless spin-2 gravitons + 2 modes eaten by spin connection.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain what a tetrad is physically, how fermion condensation produces it, why GL(4,ℝ)/SO(3,1) gives the right mode count, and what the 4 structural obstacles are for emergent fermions
vertices.example: Paper 5 (ADWMechanism.lean, 21 theorems). gap_equation.py computes the Coleman-Weinberg V_eff and critical coupling G_c.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Vestigial Gravity (Level 1)
vertices.description: Volovik's proposal: even without a coherent tetrad VEV, the composite metric correlator g_μν = η_ab⟨E^a_μ E^b_ν⟩ can have Lorentzian signature — producing bosonic Einstein GR without tetrads. The three-phase structure: pre-geometric → vestigial → full tetrad. EP violation predicted.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the difference between Level 1 (vestigial) and Level 2 (full tetrad) gravity, what a composite order parameter means, why EP violation occurs, and what the Monte Carlo simulation found
vertices.example: Paper 6. monte_carlo.py and phase_diagram.py implement the lattice simulation. VestigialGravity.lean has structural theorems.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Coleman-Weinberg Effective Potential
vertices.description: One-loop quantum corrections to the classical potential: the fermion determinant det(∂̸ + e·γ·∂) gives V_eff[e]. SSB occurs when the radiatively generated minimum is away from the origin. Critical coupling G_c = 8π²/(N_f Λ²).
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain what 'integrating out fermions' means physically, how radiative corrections can trigger symmetry breaking, and what the critical coupling represents
vertices.example: gap_equation.py computes V_eff via the Coleman-Weinberg mechanism. The Hubbard-Stratonovich decomposition in hubbard_stratonovich.py sets this up.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Fracton Hydrodynamics & Information Retention
vertices.description: Fractons are quasiparticles with restricted mobility (cannot move in isolation). Fracton hydrodynamics conserves charge + dipole moment + higher multipoles, retaining exponentially more UV information than standard Navier-Stokes. The SK-EFT for fracton hydro (Glorioso et al.).
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain what restricted mobility means physically, why conserving more charges retains more information, how fracton hydro connects to the string-net → fracton chain, and why fracton hydro still cannot carry non-Abelian gauge info
vertices.example: sk_eft.py and information_retention.py. FractonHydro.lean formalizes conservation laws and information bounds.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: String-Net Condensation & Topological Order
vertices.description: Levin-Wen's framework: condensing extended string-like objects on a lattice produces topological order, emergent gauge fields, and emergent fermions. The UV origin for gauge structure in the hybrid architecture. Works in 2+1D; 3+1D is string-membrane-nets.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the basic idea of topological order (ground state degeneracy depending on topology), how string condensation produces gauge fields, and why this is the architecture's Layer 1
vertices.example: The Critical Review v3 §4 discusses the three-layer hybrid architecture. String-nets are Layer 1, providing non-Abelian gauge structure that bypasses the fluid layer entirely.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: The Three Structural Walls
vertices.description: The three fundamental obstructions for the fluid-based approach: (1) Non-Abelian gauge wall — structurally impossible at fluid layer (gauge erasure theorem). (2) Dynamical gravity wall — Nordström ceiling for bosonic systems; ADW route needs fermions. (3) Chirality wall — fracturing but not broken (TPF disentangler, SMG at 16 Weyl).
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can articulate each wall precisely, explain what would change the picture for each, and assess the current status with nuance (not just 'blocked' or 'open' but the actual state of play)
vertices.example: Critical Review v3 §2 provides the definitive assessment. Each wall is addressed by specific phases of the program.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: The Chirality Wall & Lattice Fermions
vertices.description: Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem: chiral fermions cannot exist on a lattice with standard assumptions. The TPF symmetry disentangler (Jan 2026) evades the no-go by using infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The Golterman-Shamir generalized no-go. SMG evidence at 16 Weyl fermions.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem intuitively, what the TPF construction does differently, the three critical gaps (4+1D conjecture, gauging step, 2D→4D), and why this matters for the program
vertices.example: tpf_gs_analysis.py and ChiralityWall.lean. Phase 4 Wave 1 item 1B.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: BEC Experimental Landscape
vertices.description: Steinhauer (Technion, ⁸⁷Rb): the only Hawking measurement, unreplicated. Heidelberg (³⁹K, Feshbach tunability): best for κ-scaling test. Trento (²³Na spin-sonic): qualitatively different. Paris polariton: observed negative-energy modes. Platform-specific predictions from the SK-EFT.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can articulate the experimental status, why independent replication matters, what each platform offers uniquely, and how the SK-EFT predictions distinguish platforms
vertices.example: predictions.py produces platform-specific spectral tables. prediction_tables.tex is the standalone prediction document.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Backreaction & Acoustic BH Evolution
vertices.description: Hawking radiation extracts energy from the horizon, modifying the background flow. Acoustic BHs cool and approach extremality (opposite of Schwarzschild). Backreaction timescale computable for each platform. Connection to Balbinot et al. 2025.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain why acoustic BHs cool instead of heating up (unlike Schwarzschild), what extremality means, and why this matters for experimental observation time
vertices.example: backreaction.py computes the evolution. The analog of the Page curve.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Volovik's He-3 Program & Superfluid Classification
vertices.description: Superfluid ³He-A has topologically stable Weyl point nodes producing emergent Weyl fermions, gauge fields, and tetrad gravity. The master classification: tensor rank → graviton spin; momentum-space topology → gauge/Weyl; statistics → mechanism availability.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the classification table physically, why scalar order parameters give spin-0 gravity while tetrads give spin-2, and what ³He-A demonstrates experimentally
vertices.example: Critical Review v3 §3 Master Classification Table. ginzburg_landau.py extends the He-3/ADW analogy.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Reading Lean Proofs for Physical Insight
vertices.description: Using the Lean formalization not just as verification but as a source of physical insight: when a proof is trivial (rfl), the physics is definitional; when it requires contradiction, there's a non-obvious constraint; when Aristotle needs 15 lines, the result is genuinely nontrivial.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can look at a Lean theorem and its proof and extract physical insight about what the proof structure tells you about the physics
vertices.example: The FDR γ₁ sector proved by 'unfold; aesop' vs the uniqueness theorem requiring 15 lines — the former is trivially true by construction, the latter encodes a genuine constraint.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: The Three-Layer Hybrid Architecture
vertices.description: The fluid-based approach to fundamental physics as a three-layer model: Layer 1 (quantum order, UV) → Layer 2 (fluid dynamics, mesoscopic) → Layer 3 (Standard Model + GR, IR). What each layer provides, what cannot pass between layers, and the honest minimum viable hybrid.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can articulate the architecture, explain what it achieves and what it cannot do, and assess the revised scorecard from Critical Review v3 §4 with genuine understanding
vertices.example: Critical Review v3 §4 and Feasibility Study §3. The honest minimum viable hybrid: fermionic p-wave superfluid → Landau hydro → Diakonov tetrad gravity.

frequency_analysis.analysis_notes: This is a 75/25 domain: the top 8 components (EFT philosophy, acoustic metric, SK contour, SSB, Hawking radiation, dissipative correction, SK axioms, KMS/FDR) account for ~60% of the required competence. The gateway nodes are EFT philosophy (unlocks all EFT reasoning), acoustic metric (unlocks all analog gravity), SK contour (unlocks all dissipative physics), and SSB (unlocks both superfluid EFT and emergent gravity). The dissipative correction is the central node — it synthesizes the acoustic metric + SK formalism streams into the program's main result. Phase 3-5 topics (gauge erasure, ADW, fracton, chirality) are important but more modular — they branch off the main trunk rather than forming a linear chain.

transfer_pathways.description: As architect of the entire program, you already know WHAT the dissipative correction is and HOW it was derived. The transfer gap is WHY — physical intuition for why each step in the derivation is inevitable rather than arbitrary.
You articulated the three walls in the Critical Review. The gap is moving from a documented assessment to felt understanding of the obstruction mechanisms.
You designed the architecture. The gap is intuition for WHY each link works and where the weak joints are.
You understand EFT concepts through the project. The gap is the visceral feel for what the derivative expansion physically means — why higher-order terms are literally 'smaller physics.'
You know Son's EFT from the project but building intuition for WHY L=P(X) is the unique answer requires deeper comfort with symmetry arguments.
You understand the acoustic metric formula. The gap is feeling how it emerges inevitably from linearized fluid equations — the geometric perspective.
You know the formula T_H = ℏκ/2πk_B and the basics. Building intuition for WHY horizons radiate — the mode-mixing picture — will deepen quickly given your GR background.
You've worked extensively with BEC parameters through the code. The gap is physical intuition for what's happening microscopically — why atoms condense, what the healing length physically represents.
You know the FDR and KMS from the SK context, but the general stat mech foundations (partition functions, ensemble theory, entropy) need dedicated building.
You know the concepts but haven't internalized the variational principle intuitively. This is a foundation that will pay dividends across everything.
You're expert-level with Lean. The curriculum will teach you to extract PHYSICAL insight from proof structure — a new dimension of your existing skill.

CAUTION: The Lagrangian formalism in EFT is DIFFERENT from classical mechanics in emphasis. In classical mechanics, you solve the equations exactly; in EFT, you systematically ignore UV physics. The mental habit of 'finding the exact solution' must be replaced by 'what's the leading-order answer and why is it sufficient.'

failure_points.description: PROJECT FAMILIARITY ≠ PHYSICS UNDERSTANDING. The biggest risk: confusing knowing the results, terminology, and narrative of the research program with understanding the physics. You can explain that δ_diss = Γ_H/κ without feeling WHY. This illusion is especially strong because you can talk fluently about the work.
failure_points.mitigation: The Feynman test: can you explain this to someone who doesn't know the project? Not by reciting results but by building the physics from scratch. If you find yourself reaching for project-specific language instead of physical reasoning, the understanding is structural but not intuitive.

failure_points.description: THE FORMALISM WALL. Around weeks 3-5, when we dive deeper into the SK formalism and EFT structure, there's a natural plateau where the formalism starts to feel like abstract symbol manipulation rather than physics. This is where many self-taught physicists stall.
failure_points.mitigation: Every formal statement gets a physical thought experiment. 'What would happen if KMS was violated?' 'What does a negative imaginary part of the action physically mean?' Tie every formula back to an observable — something an experimentalist could measure.

failure_points.description: FROM SEQUENTIAL TO STRUCTURAL. Around weeks 6-8, the curriculum transitions from the Phase 1-2 linear narrative to the branching Phase 3 topics. This requires shifting from 'follow the derivation step by step' to 'understand how gauge erasure, WKB, and ADW are three independent consequences of the same foundations.' Learners who stay in sequential mode get lost.
failure_points.mitigation: Explicit architecture sessions: before diving into Phase 3 topics, spend a session mapping how they connect to the foundation and to each other. Use the hybrid architecture as a unifying frame.

failure_points.description: CONFUSING THE MAP FOR THE TERRITORY. Treating the classification of the three structural walls as fixed verdicts rather than living assessments that could shift with new results. The walls are provisional — the chirality wall was 'blocked' a year ago and is now 'fracturing.'
failure_points.mitigation: Frame each wall session around 'what would change this?' rather than 'what is the current status.' The physicist's instinct is to look for the crack, not to memorize the verdict.

failure_points.description: THE GRAVITY WALL CONCEPTUAL LEAP. Understanding vestigial gravity and the ADW mechanism requires a genuine conceptual leap: spacetime geometry as an emergent composite order parameter, not a fundamental substrate. Many physicists never make this leap because it requires letting go of geometric intuition.
failure_points.mitigation: Use the He-3 analogy extensively — real physical systems where geometry emerges from fermionic order parameters. Walk through the GL phase classification to make the abstract concrete.
